newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS --up 3/8, but supply pressure hits.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS --up 3/8, but supply pressure hits.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were up about 3/8 point late Wednesday, but participants said the market was having trouble clearing recent new issue deals.
Minnesota's $215 million offering, won Tuesday by Prudential Securities, was the most frequently mentioned sticking point. Market sources said the balance was roughly $91 million and moving slowly.

Wednesday's big competitive deal, a $250 million general obligation issue from Maryland, had about $48 million left in the account's 2009 through 2011 maturities. But market sources said many of the deal's other bonds remained in dealers' hands, a sign of demand problems.
Lehman Brothers won the Maryland issue, and reoffered the 2011 maturity at a 4.80 percent yield.

The negotiated sector was also active, with PaineWebber Inc repricing the day's largest offering, a $334 million California Department of Water Resources issue. The deal carried a top yield of 5.28 percent in 2028.
Treasury prices were up more sharply than munis, with the yield on the long bond falling to levels not seen since February. The 30-year bond gained 27/32 to 103-31/32, to yield 6.33 percent.

A key market focus continued to be Friday's jobs report for June, which was expected to show a gain in non-farm payrolls of 193,000 and a drop in the unemployment rate to 4.9 percent from 5.0 percent.
In the muni secondary market, bids on Fairfax County Water Authority, Va., 5.0s of 2029 were bid at 5.28 percent, down two basis points from Tuesday.
Harris County, Texas, MBIA Toll Road 5.0s of 2021 were bid at 5.25 percent, down three basis points.

In futures, September municipal bonds rose 16/32 to 122-2/32, while September Treasury bonds gained 14/32, moving to 116-12/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts widened to 182 ticks from 180 at the close on Tuesday.
Municipal bond sales for Thursday were expected to total $979 million in 16 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totalled $761 million in five sales, with a $640 million E-470 Highway Authority, Colo., offering through Lehman Brothers topping the list.
On the competitive side, 11 sales totaling $218 million were scheduled. A $101 million Wisconsin offering at 1100 EDT was the largest.
